subject: Orchid Labs Sandbox POC: solution synthesis & ops handoff
content:
From: Suresh Rao <suresh@orchidlabs.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Labs EngOps <engops@orchidlabs.io>, Chris Park <chris@cloudforge.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid sandbox POC kickoff + initial scope

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for agreeing to run a short sandbox POC with us. The high-level goal is to validate a joint reference design where Orchid routes inference through Redwood Dedicated for production-like telemetry and then falls back to a smaller local model during simulated congestion. We want to exercise:

- Network connectivity (VPC peering + egress policies)
- Model variant routing and fallback behavior
- KV/prefix caching correctness with session continuity
- Telemetry (per-request latency/cost traces)

Attached is a proposed scope and a quick network sketch. Can Redwood provide:

1) a short runbook we can follow for environment setup (VPC setup, firewall rules, expected test accounts)
2) acceptance criteria for the POC (latency SLOs, failure modes)
3) an initial PX/sandbox token and a point-of-contact for on-call during the test window May 10-12?

Cheers,
Suresh
Principal Engineer, Orchid Labs
[attachment: orchid-poc-scope.pdf (pdf)]

-----Original Message-----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Rao <suresh@orchidlabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid sandbox POC kickoff + initial scope

Thanks Suresh — excited to run this with you. Quick answers and next steps:

- We attached a lightweight "Redwood sandbox playbook" that covers VPC peering steps, expected IAM roles, and a checklist for creating the test workload. (orchid-poc-scope.pdf + redwood-sandbox-playbook.md)
- Acceptance criteria proposal:
  * 95th percentile token latency under normal load <= 220ms
  * Fallback correctness: <0.1% session split errors when triggering model-variant fallback
  * Telemetry: every request logs trace_id and model_variant with cost estimate
- I'll assign Mateo as the technical lead for setup and Karthik to own network/security validation. Marissa will coordinate scheduling and partner comms.

Can you confirm the sample traffic profile (tokens/sec, concurrency) you expect to run? If May 10-12 still works we'll do a dry run May 9 with a short smoke test.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-sandbox-playbook.md (md)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Suresh Rao <suresh@orchidlabs.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid sandbox POC kickoff + initial scope

Quick technical notes from the infra side:

- For model-variant fallback we recommend running two model replicas: a full-precision medium LLM on Redwood Dedicated and a quantized small LLM local to Orchid (local adapter). We'll validate KV cache TTLs and prefix cache consistency across variants.
- Network: we'll need VPC peering and an egress NAT IP — provide the Orchid side CIDR and the firewall rule owner.
- Metrics: please add the following tags to requests during the run: environment=orchid-poc, partner=orchid, test-run=may-10-dryrun

I'll prepare a short acceptance script (curl-based) that validates both routing and expected trace fields.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Suresh Rao <suresh@orchidlabs.io>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 12:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid sandbox POC kickoff + initial scope

Looping in a couple of security checks we'll run during onboarding:

- Verify TLS termination points and mutual TLS where devices require it
- Confirm data retention and log forwarding scope (we will not persist inputs beyond POC unless explicitly agreed)
- Validate KMS integration for any customer-managed keys needed for tokens

Soojin/Marissa: I suggest adding a short line in the scope doc specifying the log retention policy for the sandbox to avoid confusion.

-Karthik

From: Suresh Rao <suresh@orchidlabs.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid sandbox POC kickoff + initial scope

Thanks all — confirmed:

- Orchid will provide CIDR and an alias (eng-test@orchidlabs.io) by EOD May 4.
- Dry run May 9 09:00-11:00 PT confirmed (we saw the invite).
- Acceptance criteria look good; one ask: can Redwood add a short fallback acceptance test that asserts session continuity across variant switch? We can run it during the dry run.

Appreciate the quick turn — looking forward to the dry run.

Best,
Suresh
Principal Engineer, Orchid Labs
